learningObjective: Compute the largest square tile size for a GEMM inner kernel so that the three FP32 tiles fit within a target L1/SMEM budget.

canonicalClaims.claim: For square FP32 GEMM tiling with three T×T tiles sharing an on-chip buffer of B bytes, the largest legal tile size satisfies 12·T² ≤ B, i.e., T ≤ √(B/12).
conditions: The three tiles occupy the buffer exclusively.
nonImplications: Does not imply the largest fitting T is the best-performing T; register-tiling, warp shape, and reuse pattern still matter.
Does not imply the same formula holds for FP16/BF16 tiles (12·T² becomes 6·T²).

misconceptions.claim: Caches or shared memory buffers tolerate 2× to 4× overcommit; the reported budget is a soft limit.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Overcommitting the on-chip budget forces either eviction thrashing (caches) or a static allocation error (SMEM).
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA Programming Guide, shared memory allocation

misconceptions.claim: The tile size should always be chosen as small as possible to guarantee cache residency.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Too-small tiles reduce arithmetic-intensity gains from tiling and increase loop-overhead / launch counts.

misconceptions.claim: Only the A and B tiles need to fit; C_tile is 'accumulated in registers' and does not count toward the budget.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In the SMEM-tiled formulation, C_tile is held in the block's memory; ignoring it under-counts the footprint by 33%.

misconceptions.claim: For FP16 tiles the largest T is the same as for FP32 because the formula is dtype-agnostic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Element size halves for FP16, so T grows by √2; the formula is 6·T² ≤ B in FP16.

implementationFacts: sm_80 configurable L1/SMEM allows up to 164 KB SMEM per SM but per-block SMEM has separate limits.
TensorIR / MetaSchedule automates the search over tile sizes subject to a memory budget.
performanceScenarios: For a 48 KB budget in FP16, T can go up to 90 (round to 88 for warp alignment).
Choosing T slightly below the maximum is common to leave room for double-buffering (2× tile A + 2× tile B).
